title: Descents
key_idea: The **Eulerian number** $A(n,k)$ (also written $\langle\begin{smallmatrix}n\\k\end{smallmatrix}\rangle$) counts permutations of $[n]$ with exactly $k$ descents. Their generating function is the **Eulerian polynomial** $A_n(t) = \sum_k A(n,k) t^k$. These satisfy the recurrence $A(n,k) = (k+1)A(n-1,k) + (n-k)A(n-1,k-1)$ and the 'worpitzky identity' connecting Eulerian numbers to power sums.
summary: **To be filled in when you reach this section.** Key results: Eulerian recurrence, symmetry $A(n,k) = A(n, n-1-k)$, the EGF $\sum_n A_n(t) x^n/n! = (t-1)/(t-e^{(t-1)x})$, the Worpitzky identity $n^k = \sum_j A(k,j)\binom{n+k-j-1}{k}$, and the connection to descent sets in §2.2.

notation.description: Eulerian number: number of $w \in S_n$ with exactly $k$ descents
Number of descents of $w$: $|\{i \in [n-1]: w(i) > w(i+1)\}|$
Eulerian polynomial $\sum_{k=0}^{n-1} A(n,k) t^k$; also written $\sum_w t^{\text{des}(w)}$
